domains.learnerSummary: You will learn to use the digital tools of university study, including learning platforms, word processing, reference managers, shared documents, translation and feedback tools, efficiently, critically and within your institution’s rules.

stageEmphasis.foundation: Orientation to the learning platform, file management and word processing, with transparent and critical use of machine translation.
stageEmphasis.pre-sessional: Institutional systems and policies, reference managers, machine translation and automated feedback as supports, and digital collaboration in project work.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-ug: Efficient assignment workflows: styles, reference managers, shared documents and critical use of feedback tools.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-pgt: Managing dissertation-scale work: versioning, reference libraries, collaboration and supervisor feedback in shared documents.
stageEmphasis.pgr: Thesis-scale document management, research data and file organisation, and a professional online presence.

domains.name: Generative AI Literacy
domains.summary: Generative AI literacy is treated here as part of academic literacy: understanding how large language models generate text and why they fail; reading and applying AI policies that vary by institution, module and task; acknowledging and verifying AI use; and using AI in ways that build rather than replace learners' own language, reasoning and voice. The domain also covers the limits of AI-text detection, including documented bias against writers using English as an additional language, and privacy and intellectual-property risks. Tools and policies change quickly, so topics are framed around durable principles and verification habits rather than particular products.
domains.learnerSummary: You will learn how generative AI tools work and where they fail, and how to find out what AI use is allowed in each task. You will also practise acknowledging and checking AI use, using AI to develop your English while keeping your own voice, and responding if a detector wrongly flags your work.

stageEmphasis.foundation: How generative AI works and fails, finding the AI rules for each task, and using AI for explanation and practice rather than to produce assessed text.
stageEmphasis.pre-sessional: Transparent, policy-compliant AI use in source-based assignments, verifying outputs and references, and keeping evidence of one's own writing process.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-ug: Module-specific rules, acknowledging use, and evaluating AI as a language and study resource within the discipline.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-pgt: AI in literature searching and summarising, authorship and voice in extended writing, and data privacy in dissertation research.
stageEmphasis.pgr: AI research tools, publisher and funder policies, research data privacy and intellectual property, and authorship norms in publication.

domains.name: Science, Engineering & Computing
domains.summary: This domain covers the discourse of the natural sciences, engineering, mathematics and computing: how technicality, nominalisation and taxonomies build scientific knowledge, and how learners produce explanations, protocols and specifications, experimental language, proofs and software documentation. These fields are typically 'hard' in Becher and Trowler's terms, with cumulative knowledge, high consensus on method and texts in which visuals, notation and code carry much of the meaning. Teaching works best when EAP staff analyse departmental exemplars with subject lecturers, because conventions differ between, for example, a chemistry protocol, a civil engineering specification and a computing README.
domains.learnerSummary: You will learn how scientists, engineers, mathematicians and programmers use English to explain, instruct, specify, prove and document, and how to write these texts the way your department expects.

stageEmphasis.foundation: Build control of scientific explanation, process description and experimental vocabulary alongside subject content, using textbook and practical-class texts.
stageEmphasis.pre-sessional: On science and engineering pathways, raise awareness of nominalisation, technicality and explanation genres, and practise reading and writing short experimental and procedural texts.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-ug: Embed work on lab-related language, specifications, proofs and documentation in modules, ideally co-designed with subject staff around real assignments.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-pgt: Focus on precision in specifications, design documentation and project reports, and on the conventions of the student's specialism.
stageEmphasis.pgr: Support protocol and methods writing, documentation of research software and the conventions of mathematical and technical publication.

domains.name: Health & Life Sciences
domains.summary: This domain covers the literacies of nursing, medicine, allied health, pharmacy and related life-science programmes, where academic writing is tied to professional practice and patient safety. Its topics are evidence-based practice as an organising concept, reflective practice writing, case presentations and care plans, communication on placement, and critical appraisal. Many of these genres are assessed against professional standards as well as academic criteria, so EAP teachers should work with clinical educators, use anonymised local exemplars and check regulator and programme requirements on confidentiality and record-keeping.
domains.learnerSummary: You will learn how health professionals use evidence, reflect on practice, document and present patient care, appraise research and communicate safely with patients and colleagues in English.

stageEmphasis.foundation: Introduce evidence-based practice and the vocabulary of health care in foundation programmes that lead to health degrees.
stageEmphasis.pre-sessional: On health pathways, prepare students for reflective writing and for spoken communication with patients and colleagues.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-ug: Embed support for reflective assignments, care plans, case studies and placement communication in nursing, midwifery, medicine and allied health programmes.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-pgt: Emphasise critical appraisal, evidence synthesis and reflective writing for experienced practitioners taking master's degrees.
stageEmphasis.pgr: Support systematic review writing and reporting to recognised reporting guidelines.

domains.name: Business & Economics
domains.summary: This domain covers the literacies of business, management and economics programmes, which together attract large numbers of international students on foundation, UG and PGT courses. Business schools assess many simulated professional genres (case analyses, reports, memos, pitches) that are oriented to decision-makers, while economics builds arguments from models, assumptions and conditional reasoning. Nathan (2013) and Zhu (2004) show that these assignment genres differ from the academic essay in purpose, structure and reader, so EAP teaching should analyse the assignment briefs and exemplars of the specific school with subject staff.
domains.learnerSummary: You will learn how to analyse business cases, use management frameworks critically, reason with economic models and write the reports, memos and pitches that business schools assess.

stageEmphasis.foundation: Introduce management frameworks, case analysis and the language of economic models within business foundation programmes.
stageEmphasis.pre-sessional: On business pathways, contrast the business report and case analysis with the academic essay and practise frameworks applied to short cases.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-ug: Embed support for case analyses, reports and economic reasoning in modules, using the school's own briefs and exemplars.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-pgt: Support the high volume of case-based and professional genres on master's programmes such as the MBA and MSc Management, where students often have little time to adjust.

domains.name: Law
domains.summary: This domain covers the literacies of studying law in English, with a primary focus on common-law systems such as England and Wales: the register and terms of art of legal English, reading and briefing cases, reading legislation, answering problem questions and writing legal essays. Legal knowledge is constructed through authoritative texts (judgments and statutes) whose language is itself the object of analysis, so reading precision and the handling of authority are central (Bhatia, 1993; Twining & Miers, 2010). Many international law students, especially on LLM programmes, have trained in civil-law or mixed systems, which makes making the common-law conventions explicit particularly important.
domains.learnerSummary: You will learn how to read cases and legislation, use legal terms precisely, answer problem questions and write legal essays supported by legal authority and the referencing style your law school requires (often OSCOLA in the UK).

stageEmphasis.foundation: Introduce legal vocabulary, the structure of cases and the idea of precedent in law foundation programmes.
stageEmphasis.pre-sessional: On law pathways, practise reading short judgments and statutes and contrast problem questions with essays.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-ug: Embed support for case briefing, problem questions and essays in first-year LLB modules, where the conventions are new to everyone.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-pgt: Support LLM students, many trained in other legal systems, to read common-law materials efficiently and write analytical legal essays with OSCOLA referencing.

domains.name: Social Sciences & Education
domains.summary: This domain covers the literacies of sociology, politics, social policy, international relations, psychology's more interpretive traditions, education and related fields. These are 'soft' disciplines in Becher and Trowler's terms, where key concepts are contested, several research paradigms coexist and writers are expected to justify their conceptual and methodological choices explicitly. The topics address working with contested concepts, qualitative research writing, policy analysis and methodology justification, which recur from UG coursework to doctoral theses. Because expectations vary between fields and between supervisors, analysis of local exemplars with subject staff is essential.
domains.learnerSummary: You will learn how social scientists and education researchers define contested concepts, justify their methods, write up qualitative research and analyse policy.

stageEmphasis.pre-sessional: On social science pathways, introduce contested concepts and the idea that definitions and methods must be justified.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-ug: Support concept work, policy analysis and the methods and findings chapters of final-year projects.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-pgt: Focus on methodology chapters, qualitative findings and policy analysis in master's dissertations, where many students are new to the paradigms of the field.
stageEmphasis.pgr: Support doctoral researchers in articulating paradigms, operationalising concepts and writing extended interpretive analysis.

domains.name: Humanities
domains.summary: This domain covers the literacies of literary studies, history, philosophy, religious studies, classics and related fields, where knowledge is built through interpretation and argument about texts, sources and ideas rather than through accumulating findings. Becher and Trowler characterise these 'soft-pure' fields as reiterative and interpretive, and Hyland (2004) shows that their writing typically has more explicit authorial presence and evaluative engagement with sources than the sciences. The topics cover close reading, working with primary sources, interpretive argument and philosophical writing, all of which reward detailed engagement with language and a sustained individual voice.
domains.learnerSummary: You will learn how to analyse texts closely, work with primary sources, argue for an interpretation with textual evidence and write philosophical arguments with objections and replies.

stageEmphasis.foundation: Introduce close reading and the use of quotation as evidence on humanities foundation programmes.
stageEmphasis.pre-sessional: On humanities pathways, practise close analysis and the shift from summary to interpretation.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-ug: Support interpretive essays, source analysis and philosophical argument in subject modules, using the department's exemplars.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-pgt: Emphasise original interpretation, engagement with critical debates and archival or primary-source work for dissertations.
stageEmphasis.pgr: Support doctoral researchers in sustaining interpretive arguments across chapters and in archival research and citation.

domains.name: Creative Arts & Design
domains.summary: This domain covers the literacies of fine art, design (graphic, product, fashion, interior), architecture and related practice-based programmes, where much learning takes place in the studio and assessment centres on work produced, presented and explained. Language does specific jobs here: describing and interpreting visual work, presenting and defending work in critiques, and writing statements and rationales that make practice legible to tutors, audiences and juries. Schön's (1983) account of design as a reflective conversation with materials and Kress and van Leeuwen's (2006) visual grammar give EAP teachers ways to describe these practices, but the tacit vocabulary of a studio is local, so close collaboration with studio tutors and observation of crits is recommended.
domains.learnerSummary: You will learn how to talk and write about visual work, present and discuss your work in studio critiques, and write statements and rationales that explain your concept, process and decisions.

stageEmphasis.foundation: On art and design foundation courses, build vocabulary for visual analysis and confidence in presenting work in crits.
stageEmphasis.pre-sessional: On art and design pathways, prepare students for crits and for short statements about their work.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-ug: Support crit participation, design rationales and statements in studio modules, ideally with tutors present.
stageEmphasis.in-sessional-pgt: Focus on articulating a practice in relation to context and theory in statements, rationales and final crits.
